data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 never identifies what evidence within a single evaluation would distinguish a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that happens to track the right answer — the second half of the problem. Its mechanism explains WHY aggregation reduces variance, and its counterconditions list cases where the mechanism could fail, but none of them supply the requested discriminating evidence. For a task with objectively verifiable outcomes, checklist compliance that produces the correct answer is behaviorally identical to genuine reliability at the level of a single evaluation; the target would need to specify an observable signal (e.g., item-level disagreement patterns, out-of-distribution probe items, or error structure on incorrect trials) that separates mechanistic understanding from rose-tracking, and it does not.
